slides.say: For which of the following operations is a star b equal to b star a, for all numbers a and b?
Does the order of the inputs matter? [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, plugging in numbers, and then with algebra.
[short pause] Let's start with numbers. To knock a choice out, one counterexample is enough. a is one and b is two. Not equal numbers, because with a equal to b, every operation looks fine.
at: a is one and b is two

slides.say: Choice number one, one star two is two, and two star one is four. Out. Choice number two, three and six. Out. Choice number four, two and three. Out.
Choice number three, one times two plus one plus two is five, and the other way, five too. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way. What's different? Numbers can't prove always, algebra can. Swap the letters. b star a is b a, plus b, plus a. b a is a b, and b plus a is a plus b. Exactly a star b. So, not always, one example. Always, swap the letters. Choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
